title: Michelle Obama exposes Barack's annoying habit that makes her want to 'smack' him - NewsBreak
text:
By Hannah Furnell ,
8 hours ago After being married for over 30 years , there is still one thing about former President Barack Obama that drives Michelle Obama wild.
The 61-year-old divulged her husband's irritating habit, that he makes strange chewing noises with his food, while discussing their marriage with couples therapist Dr. Orna Guralnik on Wednesday’s episode of her IMO podcast.
Michelle — who shares daughters Sasha, 24, and Malia, 27, with Barack — reflected on how she and her husband often have nothing to talk about at dinner time now that they are empty-nesters, with both of their daughters having moved out.

READ MORE: Jimmy Kimmel's brutal takedown of Donald Trump in upcoming live shows
"We always have the kids to talk about, but not on a day-to-day basis," Michelle said. "We've noticed how much of our time we've spent talking about them, right? So now that we're empty-nesters, it's like, 'Well, what are we going to talk about?'"
Michelle's brother and co-host, Craig Robinson, then suggested that there is always "something to talk about" with a spouse or partner, something the therapist disagreed with. "There's a way to be next to another person, even in silence, that can be very alive," Guralnik said.
The psychoanalyst then asked Michelle to delve into what she is truly thinking about when sitting with Barack at the dinner table.
"Because how many times does somebody ask, 'What are you thinking about?' And you're like, 'Well, let me make up a thing,'" Michelle said, adding, "Because I don't actually want to tell you what I was thinking about, which is like, 'The way you’re chewing makes me want to smack you upside the head.'"
Guralnik added that this talking point would be "really interesting" to bring up, before Michelle wondered about telling Barack about her issue with him. "Why does your chewing annoy me so much? Let’s discuss," she jokingly acted out, adding. "Yeah, I don't know if I’d bring that up."
Guralnik pointed out that hearing a person chewing is the same thing as listening to the "essence" of who someone is, but at the same time acknowledged that being annoyed by chewing sounds is "a thing" in marriage. "The girls and I are very irritated with the way Barack chews," Michelle said, referring to their daughters.
Michelle's comments comes after Barack shed some light on his current relationship with his wife. The former US President was in London, where he did a speaking engagement at the O2 Arena on September 24.
The event was called An Evening with Barack Obama, and he was interviewed by historian David Olusoga. At one point, Olusoga asked Barack what he's been doing for the past few years since his last term as president, which ended in 2017.
"I was digging myself out of the hole I found myself with Michelle," Barack responded, per the Daily Mail . "Now I'm at about level ground."
His response was similar to one he made to broadcast journalist Steve Scully at another speaking engagement he had at the Jefferson Educational Society in Erie, Pennsylvania , on September 19.
Scully asked the 64-year-old how he's been spending his time. Barack replied, "Well, since I left office, I have spent over eight years now trying to dig myself out of a hole with Michelle."
"And that’s been challenging, but I feel like I’m making progress. I’m almost breaking even at the moment," he added.
